newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gehe paves way for new Lloyds Chemists bid - paper.
newsitem.headline: Gehe paves way for new Lloyds Chemists bid - paper.

text.p: Gehe AG hopes to pave the way for a fresh bid for Lloyds Chemists by providing Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) in the coming days with a list of firms interested in buying Lloyds' wholesale businesses, a German newspaper reported on Wednesday.
The British government has said bids for Lloyds by either Gehe or rival bidder UniChem can only go ahead if certain Lloyds assets are sold off.
The requirement was aimed at preventing either Gehe or UniChem from becoming too dominant in the British drugs wholesale market as a result of buying Lloyds.

Gehe believes it will take two to three weeks for the OFT and then the British Department of Trade and Industry to announce whether new bids for Lloyds can be made, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung reported.
The paper quoted the management of Gehe as saying Lloyds had given Gehe and UniChem a list of prospective buyers of its wholesale businesses.
Several of the companies were interested in buying all seven Lloyds wholesale bases in Belfast, Cambridge, Carlisle, Coulsdon, Derby, Glasgow and York -- a solution Gehe preferred, the paper said.
The paper said Gehe now hoped to be able to fulfil the requirements laid down by the British Monopolies and Mergers Commission for a bid for Lloyds.
